newsitem.title: USA: Clinton nominates Weld to be envoy to Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Clinton nominates Weld to be envoy to Mexico.

text.p: President Bill Clinton nominated Massachusetts Gov. William Weld on Wednesday to be U.S. ambassador to Mexico, a move likely to trigger a fight with a key senator that could involve Republican bloodletting.

Weld, a moderate Republican now in his second term as governor, is bitterly opposed by Sen. Jesse Helms, a conservative North Carolina Republican who objects to his support of medical use of marijuana, among other things.
As chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, which gets the first shot at ambassadorial nominations, Helms is in a position to block Weld's confirmation and has vowed to do so.
Weld, who comes from a wealthy family and entered politics after graduating with honours from Harvard and Oxford, charged last week that Helms' opposition was political.
"This is about ideological purity. And whether there is only one kind of Republican welcomed in the Republican Party ... That's what this is about," he said.
White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters on Monday that winning confirmation for Weld would require "an extensive effort on our part" to press the case for the nomination.
"It will be difficult, but we hope not impossible," McCurry said.
Weld told reporters in Boston on Wednesday he would fly to Washington next week to meet with State Department officials, and he would try to meet with several senators, including Helms.
"Our first call, I've been advised by the State Department, will be to Senator Helms, requesting an interview," he said. "The goal is the hearing."
